question: Calculate the magnitude of the tension in the tow bar.
memo:
$f_k = \mu_k N$
$= \mu_k mg$
$= (0{,}45)(1300)(9{,}8) \checkmark$
$= 5\ 733\text{ N} \checkmark$

$\sum F_x = ma_{\text{net}}$
$F_{\text{net}} = F_{\text{applied}} - f_k - T = ma$
$9000 - 5733 - T = (1300)(0) \checkmark$
$T = 3\ 267\text{ N} \checkmark$ (Accept $3\ 267\text{ N}$ to $3\ 268\text{ N}$)

The tow truck and car move at a CONSTANT VELOCITY. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the tow-truck tyres and the road surface is $0{,}45$
question: Calculate the coefficient of kinetic friction between the CAR tyres and the road surface.
memo:
For the car:
$\sum F_x = ma_{\text{net}}$
$T - f_{\text{k(car)}} = ma$
$3267 - f_{\text{k(car)}} = (950)(0) \checkmark$
$f_{\text{k(car)}} = 3267\text{ N} \checkmark$

$f_k = \mu_k N \checkmark$
$3267 = \mu_k (950)(9{,}8) \checkmark$
$\mu_k = 0{,}35 \checkmark$ (Accept $0{,}35$ to $0{,}351$)

passage: Suddenly the tow bar between the car and the tow truck disconnects and the car comes loose.
question: Using a relevant law of motion, explain why the car continues moving forward for a short distance.
memo:
According to Newton's First Law, $\checkmark$ an object continues in its state of rest or uniform motion (constant velocity) unless it is acted upon by an unbalanced / net external force. $\checkmark$
When the tow bar disconnects, the resultant/net force acting on the car in the horizontal direction is friction, thus it continues moving forward until stopped by friction. $\checkmark$

question: The coil rotates through an angle $\theta$ to a position where the magnetic flux becomes zero. Calculate angle $\theta$.
memo:
Initial magnetic flux $\Phi_i = BA \cos \theta_1$
$= (2{,}4)(48{,}6 \times 10^{-4}) \cos 0^{\circ} = 0{,}011664\text{ Wb}$
$\Delta \Phi = \Phi_f - \Phi_i$
$-0{,}005 = 0 - \Phi_i$ (using $\Delta \Phi$ magnitude or direction consistency)
$\Phi_f = \Phi_i - \Delta \Phi = 0{,}011664 - 0{,}005 = 0{,}006664\text{ Wb}$
$\Phi_f = BA \cos \theta$
$0{,}006664 = (2{,}4)(48{,}6 \times 10^{-4}) \cos \theta$
$\cos \theta = \frac{0{,}006664}{0{,}011664} = 0{,}5713$
$\theta = 55{,}17^{\circ}$
